content: Entecavir is a medication used to treat chronic hepatitis B infection, which is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus. Chronic hepatitis B can lead to liver damage, liver cancer, or liver failure in some cases. Entecavir works by reducing the amount of hepatitis B virus in the body, but it is not a cure for the infection. It is also unclear whether this medication reduces the risk of liver cancer or liver damage. Before starting entecavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Entecavir may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Additionally, alcohol may exacerbate liver problems, so it is best to avoid alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. To reduce the risk of spreading hepatitis B to others, always use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during all sexual activity. If you are pregnant, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it is not known whether it prevents the transmission of hepatitis B from mother to baby. It is also unknown if entecavir passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to your baby. Entecavir may rarely cause serious, potentially fatal side effects, including liver problems and a buildup of lactic acid in the blood (lactic acidosis). Seek immediate medical attention if you experience persistent nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness or weakness, rapid or deep breathing, unusual drowsiness, muscle pain, cold sensations in your arms or legs, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Do not stop taking entecavir without consulting your doctor, as this may worsen your hepatitis B infection. This medication is not recommended for individuals who have both HIV and hepatitis B and are not receiving effective HIV treatment. Entecavir does not treat HIV and may render certain HIV medications ineffective. An HIV test should be performed before starting this medication and repeated if there is any risk of HIV infection. When taking entecavir, follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. Do not use a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. Swallow the medication directly from the measuring spoon without mixing it with water or other liquids. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. It is crucial to take this medication exactly as prescribed and at evenly spaced intervals to maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body. Do not take more or less than prescribed or stop taking it without your doctor’s approval, as this may increase the virus level, make the infection harder to treat, or worsen side effects. Common side effects of entecavir include headache, tiredness, dizziness, or nausea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone overdoses on entecavir and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store entecavir at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Keep the medication in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
